item.title: Adopting low-cost ‘healthy’ diets could cut food emissions by one-third
item.description: Choosing the “least expensive” healthy food options could cut dietary emissions by one-third, according to a recent study.

item.title: Singapore expands emissions registry to boost corporate carbon reporting
item.description: The expanded emissions database comes ahead of a regulatory mandate for listed companies to report Scope 3 emissions this financial year.

item.title: Japan sets 2026 price band for carbon market to steer investment by big polluters
item.description: Scheme will cover up to 400 major emitters and set a floor and ceiling on CO2 prices ahead of 2027 market launch.

item.title: Asia is the world’s biggest spender on nature, but it must invest billions more: UNEP
item.description: For every $1 going to nature globally, $30 is spent on destructive activities, a new report found. Southeast Asia alone will need to increase nature financing by sevenfold annually by 2030 to meet global targets.

item.title: Asian state-owned companies dominate global carbon emissions: study
item.description: Chinese and Indian coal and oil firms accounted for about one third of global fossil fuel emissions in 2024, according to data from InfluenceMap. More than half of major Asian producers increased emissions that year, driven mainly by coal.

item.title: Indian wind and solar firm emerges in ranking of world’s greenest corporates
item.description: Suzlon Energy Ltd is the second most sustainable company in Asia Pacific, appearing in the Corporate Knights’ Global 100 index for the first time. Taiwan High Speed Rail Corp reclaims the top spot that it held three years ago.

item.title: Tougher anti-littering laws won’t clean up Malaysia without systemic reform, say experts
item.description: Without a holistic ecosystem and complementary policies, the country’s attempt to crack down on public littering through fines may only deliver short-term compliance and not lasting behavioural change.

item.title: How the Global South can deepen the benefits of Chinese clean-tech investment
item.description: Vietnam’s stalled Chinese-backed solar factories underscore how Global South nations must demand technology transfer and value addition – not just capital inflows – from China’s expanding overseas clean-tech investments.

item.title: How mountain terraces have helped Indigenous peoples live with climate uncertainty
item.description: From the Ifugao highlands to Morocco’s Anti-Atlas Mountains, Indigenous terrace farming illustrates how long-standing, locally adapted practices capture water, conserve soil and diversify crops to withstand intensifying climate extremes.

item.title: As sustainability roles get harder in 2026, burnout risk is growing
item.description: Burnout among sustainability professionals isn’t just persisting – it’s deepening, shaped by new pressures.
